market_holds: Spot $2.95-2.98 at the 52-week low, -6.7% over 5 sessions and -11.1% over 20 (sealed baseline 2026-11-20 18:09 UTC), -23.8% since 30 Sep. That fall is almost entirely the tape and the sector: FLNG -23.9% and GLNG -17.3% over the same span, and SPY -7.5% since 13 Nov (Yahoo daily bars fetched 2026-11-20). DLNG also went ex its $0.05 distribution on 13 Nov. No usable option chain, so no implied move; 20-day realised vol 30.5%, deadband 1.92%. In the last four prints the opening gaps were small: Q3-25 (20 Nov 2025, bmo) +1.4% gap / +6.5% close, Q4-25 (13 Mar 2026) +3.1% gap / -3.6% close, Q1-26 (29 May 2026) 0.0% gap / -2.1% close, Q2-26 (8 Sep 2026) +3.8% gap / +5.5% close (own arithmetic on Yahoo bars). Consensus is one analyst at EPS $0.34 and revenue ~$38.4M (aggregator snippets, date not given, so probably stale). That sits below Q2's actual $0.39 EPS and $41.2M voyage revenue. The units trade at about 1.9x annualised Q2 EPS, so the price carries heavy tail risk: Yamal Trade sanctions (34.5% of H1 revenue), UK service-provider replacement from 1 Jan 2027, steam-turbine residual values and refinancing of the sale-leasebacks in about three years. Charter cover is 100% for 2026-27. Already in the wire: the 3 Nov sanctions update, the $50M Series A redemption on 12 Nov, the US national-interest waiver of the Graham Act's Russia provisions (Oct/Nov 2026) and the EU 21st-package exemption for third-country transport.
view: The quarter is close to arithmetic. Six vessels are fully contracted and the Clean Energy charter (Rio Grande LNG, from 30 Apr 2026) is at a higher rate than before. Q1 lost 26.5 days and Q2 lost 20.5 days to unscheduled repairs, so a clean Q3 would put adjusted EPS near $0.42. Even with the same off-hire as Q2 it would be about $0.39. Both are above the single stale $0.34 estimate, so a headline beat is likely, and the last two beats opened up 1.4% and 3.8%. Against that, the line this stock really trades on is not EPS. It is the Yamal and sanctions tail and the balance sheet. The release will restate the 3 Nov sanctions language and show cash after the $50M preferred redemption, and neither is new. The $10M buyback expires 24 Nov. Last year the replacement program came separately, three weeks later, so a renewal in this release is possible but not expected. The run-in is sector and market (FLNG fell as much), so it neither proves nor disproves anything about this print. Scoring is at Monday's opening print, after a weekend, in a market that fell 7.5% in a week, on a thinly traded unit whose opening print often equals the prior close. The tape adds noise that can easily swamp a modest beat. The net is a slight upward lean, nowhere near a bet.
unpriced: Possibly the gap between likely Q3 EPS (~$0.39-0.43 on my arithmetic) and the stale single-analyst $0.34. It is small for a stock priced on tail risk rather than on quarterly earnings, and it is easily swamped by the weekend tape. No sanctions, financing or charter fact was found that the price does not already hold.

recommendation.reason: The likely headline beat versus a stale single-analyst estimate gives a mild upward lean. But DLNG trades on its sanctions and balance-sheet tail, not on EPS, and nothing in that tail is new since the 3 Nov update. The window is a post-weekend opening print in a sharply falling market on a thin unit, so the edge is far below the 65 needed.
recommendation.what_would_flip_it: Off-hire or a loss of hire on either Yamal vessel in Q3. Another possible flip is new sanctions language, such as failure to replace UK insurers before 1 Jan 2027 or an event-of-default risk, or a cut or withdrawal of the $0.05 distribution.

self_critique: The move from a Thursday bmo print last year to a Friday after-close slot, with no call, is the classic way to release unwelcome news (an impairment on the 2007-08 steam-turbine ships, a third straight quarter of off-hire, or harder sanctions language before 1 Jan 2027). Each of those would gap the stock down from a 52-week low. The 'beat' rests on one stale estimate that the market may not even watch: a stock at 1.9x earnings is not priced on the quarter. And Monday's open after a week in which SPY fell 7.5% is mostly tape. This critique argues for 50 more than for a down call, and my number is already close to it.
